title: Crypto Security
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/0/body: **Phishing** is a site, email or message made to look like a real exchange or wallet so it can steal your **password, verification code or seed phrase**. A fake site's address may differ from the real one by just **one letter**, and it can even show up at the top of Google's sponsored results.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/0/tip: Bookmark important sites and always log in from the bookmark, never from links in messages or ads.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/1/body: Scammers usually pull one of two levers: **urgency** ("Your account will be locked in an hour, confirm now!") or **greed** ("Guaranteed 5% daily profit", "Send coins, get double back"). In crypto, **there's no such thing as guaranteed profit**.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/prompt: A Telegram message: "I'm from your wallet's support team. To fix the issue, send me your 12 recovery words." What do you do?
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/options/0: Block and report them; no real support would ask for this
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/options/1: Send only half the words so it stays safe
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/options/2: Ask for their ID first, then send them
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/options/3: Take a photo of the words and send it
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/2/explanation: Your seed phrase is the key to everything you own. Giving away even half of it badly weakens your security. Real support never asks for it and usually doesn't message you first.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/3/statement: If an account with a celebrity's name and photo says "Send 1 ETH, get 2 back", it could be a real promo campaign.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/3/explanation: This is the classic "doubling" scam. No real person or company asks you to send money first to give you a prize.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/4/title: Pump and dumps and fake airdrops
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/4/body: In a **pump and dump**, a group pushes up the price of a low-volume coin and hypes it, then **dumps it** on newcomers. A **fake airdrop** shows you free tokens, but to "claim" them, you have to connect your wallet to a shady site and **sign a transaction**.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/5/prompt: This chart is a pump and dump. Tap the candle where the pump group started selling hard (the dump).
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/5/explanation: After several green candles in a row and lots of hype, a big red candle appears with the highest volume on the chart: the pumpers sold all at once onto the late buyers.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/0/meani: Fake site or message that steals your info
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/1/meani: Price pushed up artificially, then sold off suddenly
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/6/pairs/3/meani: Free tokens used to get your wallet signature
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/prompt: Someone befriends you on Instagram and introduces an "investment platform" showing 3% daily profit. Small withdrawals work at first, but to withdraw a large amount, it asks for "tax" or a "release fee". What is this?
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/options/0: A scam; the small withdrawals were just to win your trust
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/options/1: A real opportunity with a bit of paperwork
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/options/2: A reputable exchange with strict tax rules
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/options/3: A DeFi platform with guaranteed returns
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/7/explanation: This is the classic pattern of "friendship and investment" scams. The profit numbers on the site aren't real, and any money you pay for the "release" is lost too.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/8/sentence: Scammers usually work by creating a sense of ___ or stirring up ___.
lessons/defi-u1-l1/steps/8/explanation: When a message rushes you or promises unusual profit, take a step back first and check the source on your own.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/0/body: Turn on **two-factor authentication (2FA)** for your exchange account with an authenticator app or a security key. It's safer than **SMS**, because your number can be stolen with a **SIM swap**. Use a **long, unique password**, and protect your account's email with 2FA too.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/1/body: A **withdrawal whitelist** means you can only withdraw to addresses you've approved in advance. An **anti-phishing code** is a word you choose that the exchange puts in its real emails; an email without that code is most likely fake.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/2/options/0: An authenticator app or a hardware security key
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/2/options/1: An SMS code sent to your SIM card
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/2/options/2: An email code, on an email with a weak password
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/2/options/3: No 2FA, just a short, simple password
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/2/explanation: An authenticator app's code is generated on your phone itself and can't be stolen with a SIM swap. A hardware key is even tougher.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/3/statement: With a withdrawal whitelist on, even if someone gets into your account, they can't instantly withdraw to their own address.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/3/explanation: Adding a new address to the whitelist usually needs extra confirmation and sometimes a waiting period. That gives you time to react.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/4/body: A **hot wallet** (a mobile app or browser extension) is always online and handy for small, everyday amounts. A **cold wallet** (like a hardware wallet) keeps your key offline and is safer for large amounts. Keep your seed phrase **offline only**, on paper or metal.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/4/tip: To try out new sites, make a separate wallet with a small balance, not your main wallet.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/5/pairs/0/meani: Online; good for small, everyday amounts
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/5/pairs/1/meani: Offline key; good for large amounts
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/5/pairs/2/meani: Stealing your number to get SMS codes
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/prompt: You have a lot of crypto that you don't plan to move for now. Which combo is safer?
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/options/0: Cold wallet + seed phrase on paper in a safe place
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/options/1: Hot wallet + a photo of the seed phrase in your gallery
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/options/2: Exchange account without 2FA for easy access
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/options/3: Browser extension + seed phrase in your email
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/6/explanation: An offline key and an offline backup close off the two main hacking routes: malware and leaked online accounts.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps for safely setting up a hardware wallet in order.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/items/0: Buy the wallet from the official seller
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/items/1: Create a new wallet on the device itself
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/items/2: Write the seed phrase down on paper
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/items/3: Confirm the words on the device
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/items/4: Deposit a small amount first and test it
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/7/explanation: Your seed phrase must be generated on the device itself, by you. A device that arrives with a card showing a "ready-made seed phrase" is a fake.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/8/statement: If you save your seed phrase in a password-protected file in the cloud, it's completely safe.
lessons/defi-u1-l2/steps/8/explanation: Any online copy can leak if your cloud account gets hacked or malware gets in. The safest option is an offline copy on paper or metal, kept somewhere safe.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/0/body: A **rug pull** is when a token's creators suddenly **pull the liquidity from the pool**, or dump all their tokens at once, and vanish. The price drops close to zero within minutes, and holders basically can't sell anything.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/1/body: With a **honeypot**, you can buy the token, but the contract won't let you **sell**, or it charges a huge sell tax. Some contracts also let the creator **mint new tokens** whenever they want, inflating the supply.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/2/prompt: A new token's price keeps climbing, but the transaction history shows only buys, and nobody has managed to sell. What are you probably dealing with?
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/2/options/0: A honeypot; the contract is blocking sells
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/2/options/1: Natural demand; nobody wants to sell
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/2/explanation: In no real market does everyone only buy. A total lack of sells is a common honeypot sign: your money gets in, but it can't get out.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/3/prompt: Tap the candle where the creators most likely pulled the liquidity (the rug pull).
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/3/explanation: Price was climbing slowly, then crashed more than 90% in a single candle and never came back. That's the classic rug pull pattern: once the liquidity is gone, there are no buyers left to hold the price up.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/4/title: Checklist before buying an unknown token
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/4/body: Check whether the **liquidity is locked**, what share of supply sits in **a handful of wallets**, whether the contract is **verified**, and whether the owner has dangerous powers like **unlimited minting**. An **audit** is a good sign, but not a guarantee.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/4/tip: If a handful of wallets hold more than half the supply, any one of them can wreck the price with a single sale.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/5/statement: Even a project with a security audit can get hacked, or its team can dump its tokens all at once.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/5/explanation: An audit only reviews the code at one point in time. Audited projects have been hacked too, and an audit doesn't stop the team from selling its tokens.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/6/pairs/0/meani: Creators pull the liquidity and run
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/6/pairs/1/meani: A token you can buy but can't sell
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/6/pairs/2/meani: Liquidity can't be withdrawn for a set time
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/6/pairs/3/meani: Creating new tokens and growing the supply
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/prompt: A new token with these stats is being hyped in groups. What's the most sensible decision?
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/options/0: Stay out; it has several serious red flags at once
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/options/1: Go all in, because it's going 100x
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/options/2: Go in with high leverage to profit faster
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/options/3: Buy only if it's under 1 cent
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/7/explanation: Unlocked liquidity means a rug pull is possible, concentrated supply means a dump is possible, and unlimited minting means dilution is possible. A promise of sure profit is a red flag on its own.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/8/sentence: If a token's liquidity isn't ___, the creator can ___ it at any moment.
lessons/defi-u1-l3/steps/8/explanation: A liquidity lock means the creator can't pull the pool's liquidity out for a set time. Without one, the door to a rug pull stays open.
